question.text: Is every relation a function? Explain your answer and give examples.

answers.answer: No, not every relation is a function; a relation is a function only if each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection.
solution: A function needs every element of X to appear only once as a first projection.
A relation can break this if an element of X appears twice as a first projection.
Example: X = {1, 2}, Y = {3, 4}, R = {(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3)}. The element 1 has two images, so R is not a function.
A relation can also break this if an element of X does not appear at all.
Example: X = {1, 2}, Y = {3, 4}, R = {(1, 3)}. The element 2 has no arrow, so R is not a function.
Example of a function: X = {1, 2}, Y = {3, 4}, f = {(1, 3), (2, 3)}. Each element of X appears once.
So not every relation is a function.

checks.resolve_answer: No. A relation is a function only if each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection. Example: $\{(1,2),(1,3),(2,4)\}$ is not a function because 1 has two images, and $\{(1,2),(2,3)\}$ on X = {1,2,3} is not a function because 3 has no image. But $\{(1,2),(2,2),(3,4)\}$ is a function.
